title: The Dark Side of the Fan: Predicting Different Types of Fandom Elitism Through Fanship and Dark Traits Using Median Regression and Decision Tree Modelling
abstract: ABSTRACT Fandoms, or fanbases, are communities of people connected by a shared interest. Although previous studies have addressed the positive aspects of belonging to a community, this study explores the dark side of fandom engagement. This study ( n = 511) aims to examine how gender, Machiavellianism, sadism and types of narcissism (grandiose, hypersensitive and collective) predict two dimensions of fandom elitism: self‐inflation and other‐derogation. Therefore, this study addresses the knowledge gap regarding predictors of fandom elitism in niche fandoms, as previous research has predominantly focused on sports fandoms. Correlation analysis and median regression were used to establish correlates and predictors of self‐inflation and other‐derogation related to fandom elitism. A chi‐square automatic interaction detection (CHAID) decision tree model (DTM) was used to find the most influential predictors of fandom elitism. The results contribute to a better understanding of the personality profile characteristic of members of diverse Polish fandoms.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF COMMUNITY & APPLIED SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY
